message.content: {"reason": "Trusted accuracy 0.7365 with the OOF blend weight landing mid-grid (not at either endpoint) shows the DCN-MoE and HGBDT are comparable in strength but redundant: both consume the same ordinal + smoothed-TE numeric block, so TE over-smoothing on rare (coupon, occupation) cells and wrong ordinal assumptions for age/income inject correlated error into both members and averaging cannot cancel it. The cheapest high-leverage fix is a third learner occupying a genuinely different hypothesis space—axis-aligned indicator conjunctions with no integer ordering and no label-derived smoothing—plus a metric-aligned 3-way blend. These changes belong in model_design (the fitted one-hot view and ExtraTrees learner) and training_evaluation (OOF simplex search, bundle persistence, read-only predict), while CouponFeatureEngineer stays untouched because its transform already exposes every raw categorical needed and historical failures were wiring/persistence errors (fold ownership, refit-on-predict), not representation gaps.", "module": ["model_design", "training_evaluation"], "plan": {"model_design": "WHAT: Add a persistable `OneHotView` transformer and an ExtraTreesClassifier base learner as a third, structurally decorrelated member. `OneHotView` fits a sklearn OneHotEncoder(handle_unknown='ignore', sparse_output=False) over an ET-specific column set derived from the existing engineered frame: `fe.cat_cols_` (coupon, time, gender, maritalStatus, occupation, expiration, coupon_time, coupon_expiration, coupon_temp) plus the five FREQ `_ord` columns, `age_ord`, `income_ord`, `education_ord`, and `temperature` treated as *categorical strings* (float → int string), plus `BINARY_COLS` kept as 0/1 numeric indicators; it must explicitly exclude every `te_*` column and the remaining ordinal numerics so the view contains no target-derived smoothing and no integer-ordering semantics. ExtraTrees config: n_estimators=500, max_features='sqrt', min_samples_leaf=2, n_jobs=2, random_state=seed, bootstrap=False. WHY: Tree ensembles splitting on one-hot indicators make discrete conjunctions like 'coupon=Bar ∧ time=10PM ∧ direction_opp=1' that the ordinal encodings and smoothed TE systematically blur, so their residuals occupy a different subspace than the NN/HGBDT and an optimally weighted average strictly reduces variance; this directly targets the ~0.7365 plateau caused by correlated members. HOW: add `OneHotView.fit(df_out)` storing `cols_`, `categories_`, `encoder_`, `num_cols_`; `OneHotView.transform(df_out)` returns a float32 matrix (never fits); a module-level `_et_matrix(view, df_out)` that assembles the one-hot block + binary numeric block in fixed column order; and a `_fit_et(view, X, y_int, seed)` helper returning a fitted estimator or None on ImportError. Keep `_to_tensors`, `_gbdt_matrix`, `_ensemble_probs`, `CategoricalIndexer`, `CouponDCNMoE`, `MODEL_CFG`, `GBDT_CFG` and all constructor signatures byte-identical so existing call sites compile unchanged.", "training_evaluation": "WHAT: Extend the existing 5-fold StratifiedKFold(shuffle=True, random_state=42) loop and the full-data refit with an ET OOF column and a 3-way simplex blend. In each fold, after `fe.fit_target_encoding(features.iloc[tr], ...)` and `tr_out = fe.transform(features.iloc[tr])`, fit `OneHotView().fit(tr_out)` on fold-train ONLY, fit ExtraTrees on `_et_matrix(view, tr_out)` against `y_int[tr]` with seed `SEED + fold`, and write `oof_et[va] = et.predict_proba(_et_matrix(view, va_out))[:, 1]`; for the final bundle refit the view on `full_out` (before the `te_oof_train_` column overwrite is fine since ET ignores TE) and fit ET with seed `SEED + 900`. Replace the 2-way weight loop with a 3-way simplex grid (w_nn, w_gbdt, w_et ≥ 0 at 0.05 steps summing to 1) scored on OOF probabilities with the unchanged threshold sweep `np.linspace(0.25, 0.75, 101)`, always using plain accuracy on original labels. WHY: The historical TE failure was purely OOF-fold ownership and persistence semantics, so the one-hot encoder and ET must be fit fold-train-only during CV and on all training rows for the final bundle, while `run_predict` must reload (never fit) them; a simplex search is the metric-faithful way to exploit the new decorrelation instead of forcing a compromise between redundant learners. HOW: persist into the existing `bundle` dict the new keys `et_view`, `et_model`, `et_cat_cols`, `blend_w_nn`, `blend_w_gbdt`, `blend_w_et`, `has_et`, keeping `blend_w_nn` populated for backward compatibility with older bundles; keep `torch.save(bundle, ...)`, `metrics.json` fields (`oof_accuracy`, `threshold`, weights, `refit_epochs`, `n_refit`) and the `row_id,prediction` output contract intact. In `run_predict`, if `has_et` and `et_model` exist, rebuild `Xet = et_view.transform(out_df)` and `p_et = et_model.predict_proba(Xet)[:,1]`, then blend with the stored 3-way weights after renormalizing over whichever components are actually present (graceful fallback to the current 2-way or NN-only path if `sklearn.ensemble.ExtraTreesClassifier` is unavailable); keep `row_id = np.arange(n)` in authoritative input order and map back via stored `pos_label`/`neg_label`. Preserve signatures of `run_train(data_dir, model_dir)`, `run_predict(data_dir, model_dir, output_path)`, `_train_loop`, `_build_models_from_bundle`, and the argparse subcommands under `if __name__ == '__main__'`."}}

Actually engineer includes FREQ_COLS only as `_ord` and `_missing` — raw FREQ_COLS not in dfe! Check: for c in FREQ_COLS: dfe[c+"_ord"], dfe[c+"_missing"]; raw not included. So for one-hot bracket of subscription frequency, need raw values or use _ord as categorical? Plan says "subscription-frequency ... brackets expanded to indicator columns", i.e., one-hot over the raw frequency categories, not ordinal. Could one-hot the `_ord` values as categorical (still no ordering in tree splits, one-hot makes it non-ordinal). That's fine: use `Bar_ord` etc. as categorical values → one-hot. Similarly age_ord, income_ord, education_ord as categorical (one-hot) rather than numeric. That gives non-ordinal decisions and decorrelation from ordinal features. So matrix = one-hot block + binary flags. No TE, no ordinals. Good.

Also mention class_weight maybe None; ET with 500 trees and 2 jobs within time (8k rows, maybe ~100 one-hot cols; 500 trees fast enough ~seconds). min_samples_leaf=2 maybe safer; plan says 2-3. Use 3 for smoothness, but small data maybe 2. Choose 2 with min_samples_leaf=2 and max_features='sqrt'. Fine.

Blend: 3-way simplex grid search with step 0.05 over w_nn, w_gbdt, w_et; threshold sweep unchanged [0.25,0.75] 101 points. Scoring accuracy on OOF. Guard: renormalize available weights if ET/GBDT missing.

Keep seeds SEED+fold, SEED+777, SEED+900+s for ET refit maybe.
